bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar : Patna protests intensify as Prashant Kishor backs students, farmers | MorungExpress
bihar_raw_news.content: (Photo: IANS) India 25th August 2026 Patna, August 25 (IANS) Patna witnessed a tense day on Tuesday as student organisations protesting recruitment and examination issues joined farmers opposing the proposed Pataliputra Greenfield Satellite Township in demonstrations across the city. Police erected barricades at several locations to prevent student protesters from marching towards Lok Bhavan. Reacting to the police action, Bankipur MLA Prashant Kishor said recent events had demonstrated the strength of democracy. He argued that authorities now appeared to think twice before using force against protesters, describing this as a positive development. Kishor urged the government to address what he termed the legitimate demands of students and farmers, saying such concerns could not simply be suppressed. He highlighted issues including alleged privatisation and commercialisation of education, the growing influence of coaching institutes, examination paper leaks, rising unemployment and dissatisfaction among youth. He warned that failing to address these concerns could lead to larger student movements in the future. When reporters told him student aspirants were looking for him, Kishor said he was already in Patna and regularly moving around the city. Alongside the student protests, farmers from Punpun, Naubatpur, Masaurhi, Fatuha and surrounding areas demonstrated against the township project. Kishor backed their concerns, alleging that the government’s land policy could benefit major industrialists at farmers' expense. He claimed valuable agricultural land could be transferred at inadequate prices, arguing that the policy was difficult to implement in Bihar and warning that attempts to acquire large areas of productive land could lead to widespread unrest. Farmers said their agricultural land was their primary source of livelihood and that they produced three crops a year. They argued that surrendering land would threaten their families’ ability to fund education, marriages and other essential expenses. Protesters demanded the government reconsider the proposed acquisition, maintaining they did not want to surrender their land. Patna District Magistrate, SSP and SP reached the protest site and held discussions with farmer representatives, attempting to persuade them to resolve the matter through dialogue. The Bihar government has proposed developing 12 townships across the state, including the Pataliputra Greenfield Satellite Township. Farmers opposing the Patna project insist their agricultural land should not be acquired for development.

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Industrial Investment Promotion Policy 2025 is the finest in the country: Shreyasi Singh
bihar_raw_news.content: Shreyasi Singh, Bihar Minister For a politician in Bihar, the weight of past issues related to law and order remains a burden, and it requires considerable effort and time to dispel that negativity. This is particularly true for Shreyasi Singh , the state's industries minister. "Bihar has been a victim of narrative. The narrative has been set so poorly that people don't trust Bihar," Singh, who is also the state's sports and IT minister, said during a fireside chat with ET's Nidhi Sharma. "We give land of 10 acres virtually free if you are providing employment growth of 1,000; the policy is virtually the same for 25 acres. We are giving interest subvention of up to Rs 40 crore. We are giving state GST reimbursement," Singh said on the topic, 'On Target: The Youth Vote. Is India Ready for a Generational Shift in Politics?' "But, because of the narrative, there is still a hesitation in coming to Bihar. But the narrative is changing because we have the right intention along with the right policies." The legislator from Bihar's Jamui constituency is a former Olympic shooter and Commonwealth Games silver medalist in the trap event. Singh elaborated on the steps taken by her ministry to bring businesses to the state. Live Events "The Bihar Industrial Investment Promotion Policy 2025 is the finest in the country on paper. Why is there a feeling that Bihar is changing? Recently, we have been able to bring a big bag-making factory from Maharashtra to Bihar. We have managed to allot land to a manufacturer in 24 hours," she said. "Within a span of 55 days, we have taken the thought of an industry to starting production for the same. That's a record in India. That's the speed at which we are working." The second-generation politician, though, still looks at her late father-former MP and minister of state, railways and external affairs, Sanjay Singh--for inspiration. He was also the president of the National Rifle Association of India. "I saw the love and respect that people of Bihar had for my father; that is the kind of person I wanted to become. You, as a daughter or a son, are constantly comparing yourself with how great your father or mother were, and then try to fill those shoes. I don't think I'm half the person my father was. For me. He's my god," the two-term MLA said. While fondly remembering her sports career, she narrated an interesting story. "I went up to my father (who headed NRAI then) and said I wanted to start shooting and needed a gun. To which he said, "Do you think anyone who starts shooting in India starts with his or her weapon? You need to beg, borrow or ... I may be the president, but here I am you father. You need to do it as everyone else does it in India." Add as a Reliable and Trusted News Source Add Now! national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi hailed the decade-long success of the Unified Payment Interface. In a social media post, Mr Modi marked UPI as a major turning point in India’s digital payments journey. Calling on countrymen to share their UPI experience, he stated that the sheer scale and reach of UPI are something every Indian must be proud of. The Unified Payments Interface (UPI), which was launched on this day in 2016, has completed ten years of transforming digital payments in India. The unprecedented scale and reliability achieved by UPI have earned global recognition, with the system now operational across eleven countries. It has emerged as one of the most successful pillars of India’s Digital Public Infrastructure, providing an inter-operable, real-time payments platform. The UPI has surged almost 13,000-fold in transaction volume. The Finance Ministry said that the annual transaction volume increased from just 1.78 crore transactions in 2016-17 to over 24,162 crore transactions in 2025-26. The transaction value also rose sharply from 7,000 crore rupees to nearly 314 lakh crore rupees during the same time period. Our correspondent reports that by bridging the digital divide, advancing financial inclusion, and expanding access to digital financial services, UPI has empowered individuals and communities across the country while driving broad-based economic participation.

national_raw_news.title: 2 hours ago | National 90 Special bench to hear Centre’s plea on OBC creamy-layer criteria-SC
national_raw_news.content: The Supreme Court today agreed to consider setting up a special bench to hear the Centre’s plea on OBC creamy-layer criteria. The Centre is seeking clarification on the applicability of the March 11 judgment of the Apex Court for candidates of the Civil Services Examination 2025. The Department of Personnel and Training, DoPT, has sought directions allowing the government to proceed with service allocation for the 958 candidates recommended by the Union Public Service Commission. The DoPT wants the allocation to be based on the OBC creamy-layer criteria applied before the March 11 verdict. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Centre, told a bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant, along with Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana, that the DoPT had filed a miscellaneous application in a disposed-of matter seeking urgent directions. He said the matter needed to be listed before a bench headed by Justice P. S. Narasimha. Senior advocate Sanjay Hegde, appearing for a litigant, said the March 11 order had been passed by a bench comprising Justices Narasimha and R. Mahadevan. He said the miscellaneous application should therefore be heard by the same bench, as the judges are now sitting in different combinations. The DoPT’s plea arises from the top court’s judgement in the Union of India vs Rohith Nathan case in which the court, on March 11 held, among other things, that the October 14, 2004 clarifying letter could not override the September 8, 1993 office memorandum governing identification of the OBC creamy layer. The DoPT’s plea arises from the top court’s judgement in the Union of India vs Rohith Nathan case in which the court, on March 11 held that the October 14, 2004 clarifying letter could not override the September 8, 1993 office memorandum governing identification of the OBC creamy layer. The court also held that the salary or income of a parent employed in a public sector undertaking or the private sector could not by itself be treated as the determinative criterion for creamy-layer exclusion. It said, the status and category of the parent’s post, along with the prescribed income/wealth test, were to be considered in accordance with the 1993 office memorandum.

national_raw_news.title: 3 hours ago | National 77 Union Minister Piyush Goyal pitches India as global data centre Hub
national_raw_news.content: Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal today pitched India as a compelling destination for data centres saying the country is ready to work with Japanese companies to develop the sector and has already received investment commitments of worth 200 billion US dollars from large global hyperscalers. Mr Goyal said this during his meeting with Japanese Minister of Economy, Trade and Industry Akazawa Ryosei in Tokyo today. Mr Goyal, said the partnership with Japan could be summarised around four pillars of increasing trade, strengthening technology cooperation, boosting investments and promoting tourism. Earlier in the day, Mr. Goyal addressed representatives of Japanese semiconductors and artificial intelligence firms in Tokyo. Speaking on the occasion, the Minister said, the government is working on a framework to exempt high-tech sector companies, including from Japan, from mandatory Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) certification for equipment and components needed to set up manufacturing facilities in India. He said, the framework could provide exemptions at the company, industry, product or project level, depending on the requirements. He said, the objective is to ensure timely availability of equipment, goods and services for high-tech companies setting up manufacturing operations in India and support the government’s Make in India initiative. Mr. Goyal said, India is a large and growing electronics market and its semiconductor demand is expected to grow up to 150 billion US dollar by the year 2032. Mr. Goyal also held discussions with executives from Japan’s leading financial institutions to boost long-term investment and strengthen India-Japan economic ties. Mr. Goyal highlighted the strength and resilience of the Indian economy, noting that India recorded 7.7 percent growth last year despite global uncertainties and is working toward becoming a 30 trillion dollar economy by the year 2047.
